**Result:** No marine heatwaves were detected in the region (62.25–63.45 °N, 18.73–19.93 °E) for 2017-06-01 → 2017-08-31.

**What was done:**
- Downloaded all 4,120 daily files of `cmems_obs-sst_bal_phy-temp_my_l4_P1D-m` needed: the baseline pool window 1991-12-27 → 2003-01-05 (baseline years 1992–2002 plus the ±5-day spillover) and the 92 target days.
- Built per-cell, per-day-of-year pools (121 values each; 29 Feb values folded into neighbouring calendar windows; no day-60 pool), took the Hazen (type-5) 90th percentile as threshold and the mean as climatology, filled day 60 with the mean of days 59/61, then applied the circular 31-day centred moving mean — all in float64.
- Sea cells: 3,308 of 3,600 grid cells (finite SST on every target day). Hot-day runs ≥5 days with ≤2-day gaps joined → per-cell MHW mask.

**Why zero events is trustworthy:** every one of the 304,336 finite day-cell comparisons was strictly below threshold — the closest approach was −0.0031 K (2017-06-24, a single cell); typical deficits were 2–4 K (summer 2017 in this Bothnian Sea region stayed near the baseline *mean*, well below its 90th percentile). The pipeline was validated by an in-sample baseline exceedance rate of 9.1%, exactly as expected for a 90th-percentile threshold.

**Outputs written:** `output/mhw_mask.nc` (uint8 `mhw`, dims time×lat×lon = 92×60×60, all zeros, dataset coordinates) and `output/report.json` (region, baseline/target analysed spans, empty event list, `complete: true`, caveats documenting the null result).
